What Are The Side Effects of Kissing a Bearded Man? #rash While kissing a bearded man can be an intimate and enjoyable experience, it is possible for some individuals to develop a rash as a result. The presence of a beard can introduce certain factors that may contribute to skin irritation or allergic reactions. One potential cause of a rash from kissing a bearded man is contact dermatitis. This condition occurs when the skin comes into direct contact with an irritant or allergen. The beard hair itself may harbor substances such as pollen, dust, or certain grooming products that can trigger an allergic reaction or irritate sensitive skin. Additionally, the texture of the beard hair rubbing against the skin during kissing can cause friction and further irritate the skin. Another factor to consider is the presence of facial oils or bacteria that can be trapped in the beard. These oils and bacteria can potentially cause skin irritation or even infection if they come into contact with sensitive areas, such as the lips or face, during kissing. It is important to note that not everyone will experience a rash from kissing a bearded man, as individual sensitivities vary. However, if you notice any signs of skin irritation, such as redness, itching, or a rash, after kissing someone with a beard, it is advisable to consult a healthcare professional for a proper diagnosis and guidance. To minimize the risk of developing a rash when kissing a bearded man, it may be helpful to ensure good hygiene practices. #BeardRash #SkinIrritation #ContactDermatitis #AllergicReaction #SensitiveSkin #FacialHygiene #SkinSensitivity #SkinHealth #BeardCare #KissingHazards #SkinReactions #Friction #SkinInfection #SkinConditions #Dermatology #BeardedMen #SkinAllergies #FacialHair #HygienePractices #SkinProtection #doctor #medicine #interesting #interestingvideo #interestingthings #interestingfacts

Acne is a common skin condition characterized by oily skin and the presence of spots on the face, back, and chest. It occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells, resulting in the formation of whiteheads, blackheads, or pimples. Although it primarily affects teenagers, acne can occur at any age. While effective treatments are available, acne can be persistent and may even lead to scarring in severe cases. Stress acne, which resembles cystic acne with large, painful bumps containing pus, can take longer to heal and is more persistent. The main causes of acne are excessive oil production, inadequate shedding of dead skin cells, and the presence of specific bacteria on the skin. Genetic factors can also contribute to an individual's susceptibility to acne.#acne #acnetreatment #facial #facialtreatment #facialmask #charcoalmask #skinissues #skincare #skincareroutine #skincaretips #womenoftiktok #makeup #breakoutskin #tiktok

Milia removal is a cosmetic procedure in which tiny, benign cysts called milia are extracted from the skin. Milia are small, white or yellowish bumps that commonly appear on the face, especially around the eyes and cheeks. They are often filled with keratin, a protein found in the outer layer of skin. Benefits 👇  1.Improved Appearance Milia removal can enhance the appearance of your skin by eliminating small, white or yellowish bumps, giving you a smoother complexion. 2. “It’s Just a Bit of Redness, It’ll Go Down” #piercing Perichondritis is an infection and inflammation of the perichondrium, the connective tissue surrounding cartilage, often affecting the ears and nose. It can result from piercing injuries, burns, or minor trauma to the cartilage, and may lead to severe complications if left untreated. Common symptoms of perichondritis include pain, redness, swelling, and tenderness in the affected area. In some cases, there may be discharge or drainage. Early diagnosis and prompt treatment with antibiotics are essential to prevent further complications like abscess formation or cartilage damage. Severe cases may require surgical intervention to drain abscesses and preserve cartilage integrity. If you suspect perichondritis, seek medical attention to prevent complications and ensure proper healing. #Perichondritis #CartilageInfection #EarInfection #NasalInfection #InflammatoryDisorders #EarHealth #CartilageDamage #InfectionTreatment #MedicalDiagnosis #Antibiotics #CartilageInflammation #HealthcareAwareness #InfectionPrevention #EarCare #NasalCare #SkinInfection #InjuryComplications #MedicalConditions #ConnectiveTissueInfection #InfectionSymptoms #InfectionAwareness #MedicalTreatment #fyp #fypシ #medicine

“It’s Just a Bit of Redness, It’ll Go Down” #piercing Perichondritis is an infection and inflammation of the perichondrium, the connective tissue surrounding cartilage, often affecting the ears and nose. It can result from piercing injuries, burns, or minor trauma to the cartilage, and may lead to severe complications if left untreated. Common symptoms of perichondritis include pain, redness, swelling, and tenderness in the affected area. In some cases, there may be discharge or drainage. Early diagnosis and prompt treatment with antibiotics are essential to prevent further complications like abscess formation or cartilage damage. Severe cases may require surgical intervention to drain abscesses and preserve cartilage integrity. If you suspect perichondritis, seek medical attention to prevent complications and ensure proper healing. #Perichondritis #CartilageInfection #EarInfection #NasalInfection #InflammatoryDisorders #EarHealth #CartilageDamage #InfectionTreatment #MedicalDiagnosis #Antibiotics #CartilageInflammation #HealthcareAwareness #InfectionPrevention #EarCare #NasalCare #SkinInfection #InjuryComplications #MedicalConditions #ConnectiveTissueInfection #InfectionSymptoms #InfectionAwareness #MedicalTreatment #fyp #fypシ #medicine

3D facial analysing machines offer several benefits, such as: - Accurate and detailed analysis: 3D imaging technology allows for a more comprehensive and detailed analysis of the skin’s condition and structure. What can you do about sleep lines: Sleep lines, etched into the skin through nightly rituals, can be persistent and give you an aged appearance. Listen up if you are struggling with menopause and thyroid issues.  Especially if you are in UK Hello everyone, welcome to today's topic on thyroid issues and menopause.  Here’s some of the things that you need to know. Many women experience thyroid problems during menopause, and there are a few reasons why this happens. Firstly, as we age, our hormone levels naturally start to decline. This decrease in hormones can affect the function of our thyroid gland, which plays a crucial role in regulating our metabolism. As a result, some women may develop hypothyroidism, where the thyroid gland becomes underactive. Secondly, menopause can also cause changes in the immune system, making it more likely for the body to attack the thyroid gland and lead to conditions such as Hashimoto's disease. Lastly, lifestyle factors such as stress, poor diet, and lack of exercise during menopause can also contribute to thyroid issues. Therefore, it is essential to be aware of the potential impact of menopause on our thyroid health and to consult with a healthcare professional if any symptoms occur. However! 🦠 Impetigo is a common skin infection in children, particularly in the summer. It is usually caused by bacteria called Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus. These bacteria can enter the skin through a break, such as cuts, scrapes, insect bites, or eczema. 🍯 It often starts on the face as tiny blisters that burst and leave behind characteristic honey-colored crusts 🍯. Sometimes, it can also present with large blisters on the skin, known as bullous impetigo. 💦 Impetigo is usually itchy, and children scratching it can spread the infection to other areas. It is very contagious and spreads through skin-to-skin contact. It's important to wash your hands thoroughly after touching someone with impetigo and avoid sharing personal items like towels, bedding, or clothes . 💊 Mild impetigo is usually treated with antibiotic ointment, but for widespread infection, bullous impetigo, or if topical antibiotics are ineffective, the doctor might prescribe oral antibiotics. 🧴During the healing phase, soak the affected area in a bath or with a compress once a day. Use antibacterial soap, such as Dermol 500, and a clean gauze to gently massage the crusts off before applying the antibiotic ointment. Children can typically return to school or daycare 48 hours after starting treatment or once the sores have healed. #Impetigo #SkinInfection #ChildHealth  #SummerCare #dermatologist #dermatologistforkids #paediatricdermatologist  #pediatricdermatologist

Melanocytic naevi (benign moles) and malignant melanomas (all melanomas are malignant) have a few things in common. They’re both proliferation of melanocytes, a type of cell producing melanin in the skin. But while melanocytic naevi will stop its growth at some point, there is uncontrolled growth in the cases of melanomas. There’s a lot of factors at play - but the two main factors are genetics and DNA damage from UV exposure. One fact that I tell all my patients is - about 70% of melanomas will come out of nowhere (you suddenly see an odd looking lesion popping up on normal skin) and about 30% of melanomas will evolve from an existing mole (a mole that you’ve had all your life suddenly looks different and is unrecognisable). This means that all melanocytic naevi (moles) have a potential to turn into a melanoma (although the risk is very, very low for each individual mole). This is why we ask everyone to monitor their moles even if they look fine on the day of the clinic appointment. #dermatologist #dermatology #skindoctor #medical #medic #skinissues #dermdoctor #derm #skincancer #skincancerawareness #skincancerprevention #healthcareworkers #healthcareworker #moles #molecheck

In all honesty, I really didn’t know much about lichen sclerosus until I started dermatology training. In my first year as a dermatology registrar, I did a weekly vulva clinic and I was shocked to see so many patients presenting with such a long history of itchy and sore vulva. One patient reported having these symptoms for 7 years!  Lichen sclerosus is an inflammatory condition that often affects the vulva (vulva is the external part of the female genitalia- this is different from vagina) and it is very itchy and debilitating. It is one of the most commonly underdiagnosed conditions in dermatology which is a real shame because it is treatable and also treatment can reduce risk of skin cancer progression in these patients. This isn’t to say that all itchy vulvas are due to lichen sclerosus (there are many other differentials like eczema, psoriasis, irritant dermatitis, and so on) but it’s important that more clinicians are made aware of this important condition and not brush off patients as having another case of “thrush”. #dermatologist #dermatology #skindoctor #medical #medic #skinissues #dermdoctor #derm #medicine #vulvarcancer #lichensclerosus #womenshealth #meded #medicaleducation

On thing to clarify - I’ve used the term, “razor bumps” to mean folliculitis although the term is generally reserved for pseudofolliculitis (hair being trapped under the skin after close shaving). If you are getting red little bumps after shaving, it could be either infection or trapped hair follicles (or both). An aftershave wouldn’t help too much with trapped hair follicles. If you are struggling with these red bumps, I would speak to your clinician to see if they can help. As with any other skin issues, you don’t have to try to solve these problems on your own! Cryotherapy works by damaging the tissue (especially during its thawing phase) and it can be quite an easy (although stinging) treatment option for pre-cancerous lesions or benign lesions that you want gone. These pictures might look similar but their histories would have been quite different. Generally basal cell carcinomas (BCC) are slow growing lesions that might bleed every now and then - these are low grade skin cancer and generally don’t spread. Squamous cell carcinomas (SCC) would have come quite rapidly over weeks or months and grown quickly and might be sore.  These would also look different on examination. SCC can spread in some cases.
